home.metaTitle: ADHD Interactive Explorer | Understand concepts and connections
home.metaDescription: An interactive educational model for understanding ADHD terminology, context, regulation, observable behaviour, recurring patterns, functional domains, and their relationships.

hero.summary: Explore a calm, structured model of terminology, context, regulation, observable behaviour, recurring patterns, functional domains, and the scientific relationships between them.

clinical.title: Clinical definition is not the explanatory network
clinical.introduction: Formal clinical terminology describes how ADHD is defined. The wider model helps explain context-sensitive processes and observable experience. These layers are related in education, but they are not interchangeable.

anchor.label: Clinical Anchor
anchor.description: The formal symptom domains used to describe ADHD clinically.

regulation.label: Regulation mechanisms
regulation.description: Concepts that may help explain how functioning varies across demands and situations.

behaviour.label: Observable Behaviour
behaviour.description: What someone may notice happening, without treating it as proof of a diagnosis.

clinical.boundary: The Clinical Anchor stays separate: there is no mechanistic arrow from ADHD into the explanatory system.

model.title: From situation to functioning — with feedback
model.introduction: The layers offer a useful order for learning. They help you ask better questions before you open the full system map.

context.label: Context
context.description: Demands, supports, environments, and situations can change how functioning is expressed.

regulation.label: Regulation
regulation.description: Processes involved in directing attention, effort, emotion, time, and action.

behaviour.label: Observable Behaviour
behaviour.description: Concrete actions or difficulties that a person or others may notice.

pattern.label: Recurring Pattern
pattern.description: Repeated combinations across time or situations, rather than a single event.

domain.label: Functional Domain
domain.description: Areas of everyday life where a recurring pattern may matter.

feedback.label: Feedback
feedback.description: Consequences can change later context, demands, expectations, or responses.

model.caution: This is a conceptual learning sequence, not a deterministic causal chain.

network.title: Relationships are many-to-many
network.introduction: The model is a network of possible associations and influences. It does not calculate probabilities, predict outcomes, or identify one universal pathway.

behaviour.title: One behaviour, several pathways
behaviour.description: The same observable behaviour may connect with different regulatory and contextual explanations.

regulation.title: One concept, several behaviours
regulation.description: A regulation concept may be relevant to more than one kind of observable behaviour.

context.title: Context can act across the system
context.description: A situation can affect several layers and may amplify difficulty or provide support.

explore.title: Where would you like to explore?
explore.introduction: Home remains your orientation point. Start with the whole system today, or see which focused experiences are being prepared next.

map.title: System Map
map.description: Explore the complete educational network and its scientific relationships.

behaviours.title: Behaviour Explorer
behaviours.description: Begin with something observable and examine multiple possible pathways.

context.title: Context & Feedback Explorer
context.description: Explore how context can change functioning and participate in feedback.

presentations.title: Presentation Education
presentations.description: Learn current formal ADHD presentation language without inferring a presentation.

disclosure.paragraphOne: The explorer separates formal clinical terminology from a broader explanatory network. It uses progressive disclosure so you can understand the major layers before meeting all 30 canonical concepts.
disclosure.paragraphTwo: Connections represent possible associations or influences. They support education and exploration; they are not a test, personalized assessment, or claim that one path applies to everyone.
